text_blocks.snippet: Yes, there is a live attenuated flu vaccine, also known as the nasal spray flu vaccine. This vaccine, called FluMist, uses weakened (attenuated) live flu viruses to stimulate an immune response, according to the CDC. However, it is important to note that not all flu vaccines are live attenuated. The injectable flu shots are made with inactivated (killed) viruses or just proteins from the flu virus, according to Centers Urgent Care.

list.title: Live Attenuated Flu Vaccine:
list.snippet: The nasal spray flu vaccine, FluMist, contains live, weakened influenza viruses. These viruses are attenuated (weakened) to the point where they cannot cause illness but can still trigger an immune response.

list.title: Inactivated Flu Vaccines:
list.snippet: Most flu shots are made with inactivated (killed) flu viruses or with just proteins from the flu virus. These vaccines cannot cause the flu because the viruses are no longer active.

list.title: Safety:
list.snippet: Both live attenuated and inactivated flu vaccines are considered safe and effective. The live attenuated vaccine is not recommended for certain groups, such as pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems.
